item.title: News roundup from Davos Frontiers Science House Day 4 and outlook for Day 5
item.description: Frontiers Science House Day 4 underscored the urgency of turning science ambition into delivery — launching new tools to boost Europe’s competitiveness, calling for openness in research data, and exploring the disruptive potential of quantum technologies — while Day 5 turns to science diplomacy, open science, and a shared roadmap to 2035.

item.title: Whales may divide resources to co-exist under pressures from climate change
item.description: 28 years of data show that three whale species in the Gulf of St Lawrence may be dividing resources to survive in an ecosystem that’s changing under a warming climate and increased human encroachment

item.title: Frontiers Science House: did you miss it? Fresh stories from Davos – end of week wrap
item.description: Read more about the individual stories from the Frontiers Science House.

item.title: Grammy-nominated Aloe Blacc calls for open data sharing across funders and corporations at the Frontiers Science House
item.description: Speaking on 22 January at the “Novel approaches to accelerate cancer precision therapeutics—on both sides of the leash” discussion at the Frontiers Science House, the multi-platinum singer and songwriter Aloe Blacc challenged corporations and funders to open up their data to help accelerate science and its benefits.

item.title: To reach net-zero, reverse current policy and protect largest trees in Amazon, urge scientists
item.description: Current regulations in the Peruvian Amazon prioritize large trees for timber harvesting. But a new study has now shown that most carbon is stored in trees with a diameter at breast height of at least 41cm, depending on species. The authors concluded that a review of forest policy is essential to protect these trees if progress towards net-zero emissions is to be made.

item.title: 96% accurate footprint tracker for tiny mammals could help reveal ecosystem health
item.description: New footprint identification technology can identify ecosystem-critical species which were once only distinguishable by DNA.

item.title: Reducing drug deaths from novel psychoactive substances relies on foreign legislation, but here’s how it can be tackled closer to home
item.description: Guest editorial by Ric Treble and Caroline Copeland, authors of a new Frontiers in Pharmacology article that examined the impact of national and international legislation on the emergence of new psychoactive substances in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

item.title: Are cats ‘vegan’ meat eaters? Study finds why isotopic fingerprint of cat fur could trick us into thinking that way
item.description: Cats process proteins so efficiently that isotope signatures in their hair resemble plant-eaters, indicating that isotopic values alone may be insufficient to determine what animals ate

item.title: Brief, intensive exercise helps patients with panic disorder more than standard care
item.description: A key technique of cognitive behavioral therapy for panic disorder is interoceptive exposure, where patients learn to tolerate the physical effects of panic attacks through repeated simulated exposure. Now, scientists have shown in a randomized controlled trial that brief intermittent intensive exercise is more effective at reducing the severity of panic disorder than relaxation therapy.

item.title: Bison hunters abandoned long-used site 1,100 years ago to adapt to changing climate
item.description: As drought and rising organizational demands for larger hunting operations hit at the same time, ancient hunters adapted to severe droughts by shifting the way and where they hunted, study shows
